theme: The resurrection; the Great Commission, all authority, all nations
readingInstruction: Read Matthew 28:1-20. The women find the tomb empty, the risen Jesus meets them, the guards are bribed, and Jesus commissions his disciples on a mountain. This is the climax of the Gospel. Read the Great Commission aloud.
settingTheScene: Early on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary go to the tomb. Matthew’s Gospel, which began with “God with us,” ends with the risen Lord promising to be with his people always. The same Jesus who was rejected and killed now claims all authority in heaven and on earth.
observation: “And behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord, descending from heaven… rolled back the stone and sat on it” (28:2).
“He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay” (28:6).
“So they departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to tell his disciples” (28:8).
“Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they will see me” (28:10).
“And when they saw him they worshiped him, but some doubted” (28:17).
“All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me” (28:18).
“Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (28:19).
“And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age” (28:20).
interpretation:
The resurrection is announced by the angel: “He has risen, as he said.” The tomb is empty, and the grave clothes are no longer needed. The women are told to go and tell the disciples. On the way, Jesus meets them, and they take hold of his feet and worship him. Notice that he calls the disciples “my brothers,” even after they abandoned him. He is gracious to those who failed.

The guards report to the chief priests, who bribe them to say the disciples stole the body. Matthew notes that this story was still spread among the Jews “to this day.” The empty tomb was too well known to deny. The only alternative was to invent a story. The resurrection is a fact that must be explained.

On the mountain in Galilee, the eleven see him and worship, though some doubt. Jesus does not rebuke them. He draws near and speaks. His words are the climax of the Gospel. First, authority: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.” This is the fulfillment of Daniel 7:13-14, where the Son of Man receives dominion over all peoples. Then a command: make disciples of all nations. The mission that began with Abraham, “in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed,” now goes out to the world. The method is baptizing and teaching them to obey all that Jesus commanded. Finally, a promise: “I am with you always, to the end of the age.”

The book has come full circle. It began with Immanuel, “God with us,” and ends with “I am with you.” The King has conquered death, and his people are sent out in his authority and presence.
connection: Daniel 7:13-14 is the background to “all authority.” Genesis 12:3 promised blessing for all families. Romans 1:4 says Jesus was declared to be the Son of God in power by his resurrection. 1 Corinthians 15:3-8 lists the appearances. Acts 1:8 repeats the commission. Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 give Immanuel. Ephesians 1:20-22 describes Christ raised and seated above all rule. Revelation 7:9. John 20:21.
application:
Celebrate. Say aloud, “He is risen,” and let it be joy.

Think of one person you can invite or encourage to follow Jesus. Take a small step this week.

When you doubt, as some did, remember that Jesus came to them and spoke. Ask him to draw near.
prayerPrompts: Praise Jesus that he is risen as he said.
Thank him for all authority and the promise to be with you always.
Ask him to send you to someone to share his good news.
